description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of various media outlets, likely representing their proportional share within a dataset related to narrative media framing in political discourse. The chart is divided into 18 distinct slices, which are visually arranged in descending order of size in a counter-clockwise direction, concluding with an aggregated "Other" category. There is no separate legend; instead, text labels are positioned outside the pie adjacent to their corresponding slices, while numerical values—which sum to 100 and presumably represent percentages—are centered inside each slice. None of the segments are visually emphasized through explosion, offset, or bolding. Starting from the largest specific outlet and moving counter-clockwise, the slices include: Breitbart in dark blue (14), Drudge Report in brown (8), The Daily Caller in dark green (8), The Huffington Post in dark red (7), NPR in purplish-grey (6), Vox in dark brown (6), The Guardian in mauve (5), BBC in dark grey (5), RT in olive green (4), Daily Kos in teal (3), National Review in dark blue (3), Daily Mail in brown (3), Red State in dark green (3), Fox News in dark red (3), CNN in purplish-grey (3), PoliticusUSA in dark brown (3), and Shareblue in mauve (3). Finally, the "Other" category is represented by a dark grey slice with a value of 13, positioned between Shareblue and Breitbart to complete the circular chart.
